name: ElevenLabs
intro: ElevenLabs turned synthetic speech into one of the fastest-scaling AI businesses outside the frontier labs: roughly $600 million of annualized revenue by mid-2026, three years after its public beta. Here is every reported revenue, funding and valuation figure, with sources.

modelTitle: How Character Subscriptions and Voice APIs Layer Up.
modelParagraphs: ElevenLabs sells voice in two directions at once. Creators buy self-serve subscriptions billed in characters of generated speech, from a free tier up to studio plans — a cheap, high-volume funnel fed by hackathons, creator payouts and viral demos. Enterprises buy the API, where dubbing, audiobooks and real-time voice agents are billed by usage and locked in with annual commitments.

The API is where the money compounds. Once a support agent or a media pipeline speaks with an ElevenLabs voice, swapping providers means re-recording a brand, so retention holds even as model prices fall. The cost side mirrors Cursor's: inference is a real COGS line, so margin depends on running its own models efficiently rather than reselling someone else's.

faqs.a: Around $600 million of annualized revenue as of mid-2026, up from the $330 million the CEO confirmed for 2025. That implies roughly $50 million of monthly recurring revenue.
Roughly two years from its January 2023 public beta to $100 million ARR, then $330 million by the end of 2025 and about $600 million by mid-2026 — close to a doubling each year.

faqs.q: Does ElevenLabs Charge per Seat or per Usage?
faqs.a: Usage first. Self-serve subscriptions are metered by characters of generated audio, API revenue scales with dubbing, audiobooks and real-time voice agents, and enterprise contracts sit on top of the same meter rather than replacing it.
An $11 billion valuation set by a $500 million Series D led by Sequoia Capital in February 2026, more than triple the valuation a year earlier.

faqs.q: Why Do ElevenLabs Revenue Figures Differ Between Sources?
faqs.a: The 2025 figure of $330 million was confirmed by the CEO, while the mid-2026 figure of around $600 million comes from research estimates and reporting rather than an audited disclosure. This page keeps the two apart, and derived numbers such as implied MRR are labelled as estimates.
